A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DiSeNE research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, allowing retained, relocated and newly added material to be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original embedding-interpretability, link-prediction and node-classification experiments in Tables 1–3 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds benchmark comparisons, sensitivity analyses, Pareto analyses and qualitative explanation studies in Tables 1–4 and Appendices C–H.

M1.justification: The random-walk objective, attribution-based explanations, affiliation orthogonality, entropy regularization and FCAE/GAE encoders are retained. Identity inputs were already used in v1’s experiments; v2’s topology-only description and added pseudocode do not establish a changed learning procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds Tree-Cliques and Tree-Grids, extending synthetic evaluation to tree backbones and grid motifs. Appendix H also adds Cora multiclass topic classification and semantic analysis. The original real-world, biological and four synthetic datasets remain represented.

E2.justification: DGLFRM is added to the embedding comparisons in Tables 1–3 and the real-data link-prediction comparison. New Table 4 evaluates GNNExplainer and PGExplainer on GCN, GraphSAGE and GATv2 against DiSeNE explanations. These substantially broaden the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: v2 specifies plausibility evaluation on correctly classified test instances, whereas v1 describes averaging over test instances. New Table 4 evaluates only the most important embedding feature, unlike Table 3’s weighted aggregation. New protocols also include Pareto scoring, controlled regularization/depth sweeps and Cora multiclass evaluation. The principal train/test splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1’s dimensionality curves, v2 adds accuracy–interpretability Pareto analyses, sensitivity to entropy regularization and encoder depth, visual comparisons of global and local explanation subgraphs, and Cora topic/text case studies. These examine trade-offs, component sensitivity and semantic meaning that v1 did not analyze directly.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over five runs and numerical uncertainty. Appendix D newly specifies standard errors from five independent runs and incorporates uncertainty into Pareto-dominance assessment. The reported run count remains five; no additional significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Existing values change: Table 2 reports DiSe-FCAE’s PPI overlap consistency as 0.934±0.003 instead of 0.548±0.001, and Table 3 changes GraphSAGE’s BA-Cliques classification plausibility from 0.016±0.004 to 0.160±0.004. The latter table also has a revised reported evaluation restriction. Substantial new results cover added comparators, tree benchmarks, Pareto rankings, sensitivity and Cora semantics.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds a stepwise time/space complexity derivation and comparative complexity table. Appendix D defines Pareto coverage and efficiency, while Section 3.2 explicitly states the nonnegative-activation assumption needed for entropy. These supplement the formal framework; the original losses and interpretability metric formulas remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim unsupervised, dimension-wise self-explainable embeddings through structural disentanglement, introduce interpretability metrics and claim strong empirical performance. The revised abstract and conclusion make these claims more explicit, but the central contributions and their scientific scope remain the same.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly limits community alignment to one aspect of comprehensibility, discusses alternative interpretable structures, and explains attribution as marginal rather than exclusive responsibility under correlated dimensions. It also adds substantive interpretations of accuracy–interpretability trade-offs, regularization/depth effects and semantic coherence, considerably expanding v1’s qualifications and mechanism discussion.

D1.justification: v2 adds training and explanation-extraction pseudocode, DiSeNE hidden-size search details, DGLFRM hyperparameters and graph-explainer training/mask-conversion settings. It newly documents downstream attribute concatenation and Cora keyword preprocessing. These substantially expand reproducibility information; the code/data repository disclosure is retained.

R1.justification: Section 3.3 substantially expands the metrics’ positioning relative to existing explanation accuracy, contrastivity, faithfulness and BAGEL plausibility measures. Additional literature supports the new disentangled baseline, graph explainers, computational scaling and topology-versus-attribute discussion. This extends research contextualization beyond the largely retained related-work taxonomy.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are rewritten, method and metric explanations are extensively expanded, and plausibility is reorganized into explicit steps. Comprehensibility becomes Topological Alignment and structural faithfulness becomes connectivity preservation. The appendix is reorganized from A.1–A.4 into thematic sections A–H.

P2.justification: v2 adds Pareto plots, explanation subgraphs and correlation maps, sensitivity panels, semantic tables with word clouds, and algorithm displays. Existing tables gain comparator rows or task columns and are rearranged within a new journal layout. The original synthetic plots are retained and expanded as Figures A9–A12.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the interpretability claims through more relevant comparators, grid-motif tests, semantic examples, sensitivity studies and accuracy–interpretability analysis. Explicit limits on community-based comprehensibility and fuller implementation documentation address important weaknesses in v1. Some reporting inconsistencies remain: Table 2’s discussion still says DiSeNE loses on Cora despite its revised leading scores. This limits reporting precision but does not outweigh the substantial evidential and explanatory gains.
